chunks: From him, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar, from Muḥammad ibn Surūr, who said:

I wrote to Abū al-Ḥasan al-Thālith عليه السلام: What do you say about a man performing tamattuʿ with the ʿumrah up to the hajj, who arrives on the morning of ʿArafah while the people have departed from Minā to ʿArafāt? Is his ʿumrah still valid, or has it lapsed from him? Until what time does his ʿumrah remain valid if he is performing tamattuʿ with the ʿumrah up to the hajj, but he did not arrive on the Day of Tarwiyah nor on the night of Tarwiyah? So what should he do?

So he wrote back عليه السلام: At the hour he enters Makkah, if Allah wills, he performs tawaf, prays two rakʿahs, performs saʿy, cuts short his hair, enters ihram for his hajj, proceeds to the standing place, and departs with the Imam.

key_terms.الْعُمْرَةِ: the minor pilgrimage performed before hajj in tamattuʿ
key_terms.الْمَوْقِفِ: the place of standing, meaning ʿArafāt
key_terms.غَدَاةَ عَرَفَةَ: the morning of the Day of ʿArafah
key_terms.يَطُوفُ: he performs tawaf around the Kaʿbah
key_terms.يَوْمَ التَّرْوِيَةِ: the eighth day of Dhu al-Ḥijjah, before ʿArafah
key_terms.يُقَصِّرُ: he shortens his hair to complete the ʿumrah

ai.seo_question: What should a pilgrim do if he reaches Makkah only on the morning of ʿArafah while performing hajj al-tamattuʿ?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning one performing hajj al-tamattuʿ who reaches Makkah very late, on the morning of ʿArafah. The Imam عليه السلام states that his ʿumrah remains actionable at the time he enters Makkah: he completes its rites quickly, then enters ihram for hajj and proceeds to the standing at ʿArafāt.
